target.title: fix(android): stabilize Wear realtime Talk audio and tool calls
target.body:
[AI-assisted]
## What Problem This Solves

Wear OS Real-Time Talk could leave provider-selected agent tool calls unresolved, silently drop bursty Watch microphone audio before it reached the Gateway, or close the Watch audio link when a provider response exceeded the phone relay's fixed output queue. These failures could produce incorrect speech recognition, interrupted replies, or `Watch audio link is unavailable` during an otherwise valid session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The phone-side Wear realtime controller now forwards provider-selected agent consults through the phone's authenticated Gateway session, correlates the resulting run with the active relay session, and returns the final result to the realtime provider. It also preserves every accepted Watch microphone frame, queues complete provider audio events, and performs 8 KiB Watch framing inside the serial output worker instead of consuming one queue slot per chunk.

On the Watch, microphone capture is sent in 80 ms packets, playback is processed outside the Data Layer reader, and `AudioRecord` remains open while assistant audio is playing. Normal final transcripts remain direct realtime conversation and do not automatically start an agent consult.

## User Impact

Wear OS users can hold stable realtime conversations and complete intentional agent-backed requests without losing the beginning of bursty microphone input or having longer replies tear down the audio channel. The configured Phone/Gateway language remains authoritative, and the existing phone-first authentication and credential boundary is unchanged.

## Evidence

Validated on base `63f8b8454b7573c40219cfb6092e5b174e4ef87f` at refreshed head `bde38d2ebfa07188f2298c6c22ab79fa7ba120c9`.

> [!NOTE]
> ### Validation
>
> - [x] `.\gradlew.bat :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests "ai.openclaw.app.wear.WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest" --no-daemon` - PASS; 15 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors.
> - [x] `.\gradlew.bat :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest --tests "ai.openclaw.app.wear.WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest" --no-daemon` - PASS; 15 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors.
> - [x] `.\gradlew.bat :wear:testDebugUnitTest :app:ktlintCheck :wear:ktlintCheck :app:assemblePlayDebug :wear:assembleDebug --no-daemon` - PASS; 80 Wear tests, both Kotlin formatting checks, and both APK builds completed successfully.
> - [x] New regression coverage verifies that provider audio beyond the former 64-chunk limit is delivered in full and that 12 bursty Watch microphone frames reach the Gateway without `DROP_OLDEST` loss.
> - [x] Final refreshed artifacts: Phone SHA-256 `D884BC52E3D301710EBF0CF844A5C5ECDC0A97708FBB15468E4BE8FE322362D2`; Watch SHA-256 `A64239E3DE3E7A5F1E70A909EF5B2E02735030F82A23F90075691F20628EB88C`.
> - [x] `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` - PASS; the PR diff is limited to the Phone controller, its focused tests, and the Watch realtime audio client.

> [!TIP]
> ### Real Behavior Proof
>
> The repaired German realtime conversation was exercised with a matched physical Phone and Watch pair before publication.
>
> - [x] **Environment:** Physical Pixel 10 Pro XL and SM-R945F Watch running matched `ai.openclaw.app` debug builds installed with app data retained.
> - [x] **Security boundary:** The Phone remained the sole Gateway, authentication, credential, and transport boundary; no token, password, or independent Gateway identity was placed on the Watch.
> - [x] **Microphone result:** The operator-attested capture shows German Watch speech reaching the realtime conversation without the incorrect-language recognition seen before the fix.
> - [x] **Playback result:** Assistant audio completes and the Watch returns to microphone capture without a red audio-link error or session teardown.
> - [x] **Relay result:** Exact-source tests prove full delivery across both former queue-loss boundaries and preserve the existing correlated tool-call/session fail-closed behavior.
> - [x] **Proof ownership:** The physical Phone/Watch interaction and public capture were supplied and attested by the maintainer; exact-source tests, static checks, APK builds, and artifact hashes were bound locally.
> - [x] **Remaining proof gap:** The physical capture demonstrates realtime audio and configured-language behavior; provider-selected agent tool-call correlation remains focused automated controller proof rather than a second credentialed physical recording. The conflict-free final `main` refresh was re-tested and rebuilt but not recorded again.
